Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 7|LatitudeSec = 22.90 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Size = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |Artifacts = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 7|LatitudeSec = 22.90 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Size = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |Artifacts = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Shimofusazuka Kofun |image = [[File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 7|LatitudeSec = 22.90 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Size = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |Artifacts = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}} == Related Facilities == * Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum (Shirakawa City Nakata) - Stores and displays artifacts from Shimofusazuka Kofun. == References == {{Reflist}} == Sources == {{small|(Sources used for article composition)}} * Explanatory signboard (installed by Shirakawa City Board of Education) * Local government publications ** {{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=2011|chapter=|title=National Historic Site Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group (Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet)|publisher=Shirakawa City Board of Education|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}}} * Encyclopedic works ** {{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=1993|chapter=Funada Village|title={{ill|Japanese Historical Place names Series|ja|日本歴史地名大系}} 7 Fukushima Prefecture Place names|publisher=Heibonsha|isbn=4582490077|ref={{Harvid|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}}}} ** {{Cite book|editor=|author=Juntoku Kawasaki|year=1989|chapter=Shimofusazuka Kofun|title=Japanese Kofun Dictionary|publisher=Tokyodo Publishing|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Kofun Dictionary)|1989}}}} ** {{Cite book|editor=|author=Isao Suzuki|year=2002|chapter=Shimofusazuka Kofun|title=Revised Japanese Kofun Dictionary|publisher=Tokyodo Publishing|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}}} ** {{Cite Group]|title=National Historic Site Guide|publisher=Kodansha|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group (National Historic Site)}}}} - Link via {{ill|Kotobank|ja|コトバンク}} by {{ill|Asahi Shimbun|ja|朝日新聞社}}. == Related Literature == {{small|(Literature not directly used for article composition)}} * {{Cite journal|author=Jiro Iwakoshi|title=On the Ruins and Relics Near Education|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=2001|chapter=|title=Shimofusazuka Kofun Excavation Report: Fourth Survey (Shirakawa City Archaeological Report Vol. 30)|publisher=Shirakawa City Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|year=2002|chapter=|title=Shimofusazuka Kofun Excavation Report: Fifth Survey (Shirakawa City Archaeological Report Vol. Report Vol. 39)|publisher=Shirakawa City Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Isao Suzuki|year=2006|chapter=|title=Shirakawa District Government Ruins Group: A Major Administrative Center of Ancient Eastern Japan (Japanese Ruins Series 10)|publisher={{ill|Doseisha|ja|同成社}}|isbn=4886213545|ref=}}. == See Also! == * {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

{{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Shimofusazuka Kofun |image = [[File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 7|LatitudeSec = 22.90 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Size = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |Map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}} == Related Facilities == * Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum (Shirakawa City Nakata) - Stores and displays artifacts from Shimofusazuka Kofun. == References == {{Reflist}} == Sources == {{small|(Sources used for article composition)}} * Explanatory signboard (installed by Shirakawa City Board of Education) * Local It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !Construction Period |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

revision.text:
{{afc comment|1=now we have a 'Burial Facility' and 'burial goods' parameter. So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Shimofusazuka Kofun |image = [[File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 7|LatitudeSec = 22.90 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Size = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map2 = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Shimofusazuka Kofun |image = [[File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 7|LatitudeSec = 22.90 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in scale. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}} == Related Facilities == * Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum (Shirakawa City Nakata) - Stores and displays artifacts It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound Dimensions == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |LatitudeDeg = 37|LatitudeMin = 7|LatitudeSec = 22.90 |LongitudeDeg = 140|LongitudeMin = 17|LongitudeSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinatesDeg = 37|coordinatesMin = 7|coordinatesSec = 22.90 |coordinatesDeg = 140|coordinatesMin = 17|coordinatesSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |Shape = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Cultural Heritage Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Cultural Heritage Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}} == Related Facilities == * Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum (Shirakawa City Nakata) - Stores and displays artifacts
