It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !Shape !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinatesDeg = 37|coordinatesMin = 7|coordinatesSec = 22.90 |coordinatesDeg = 140|coordinatesMin = 17|coordinatesSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites part_of|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites part_of){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites part_of}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinatesDeg = 37|coordinatesMin = 7|coordinatesSec = 22.90 |coordinatesDeg = 140|coordinatesMin = 17|coordinatesSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

It is a {{ill|keyhole-typed kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-typed kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-typed, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-typed) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-typed floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Shimofusazuka Kofun |image = [[File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinatesDeg = 37|coordinatesMin = 7|coordinatesSec = 22.90 |coordinatesDeg = 140|coordinatesMin = 17|coordinatesSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |Affiliation = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinatesDeg = 37|coordinatesMin = 7|coordinatesSec = 22.90 |coordinatesDeg = 140|coordinatesMin = 17|coordinatesSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] |name = Shimofusazuka Kofun |image = [[File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |Alias = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinatesDeg = 37|coordinatesMin = 7|coordinatesSec = 22.90 |coordinatesDeg = 140|coordinatesMin = 17|coordinatesSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}} == Related Facilities == * Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum (Shirakawa City Nakata) - Stores and displays artifacts Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinatesDeg = 37|coordinatesMin = 7|coordinatesSec = 22.90 |coordinatesDeg = 140|coordinatesMin = 17|coordinatesSec = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |ConstructionPeriod = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National other_designation (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National other_designation in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National other_designation in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 7|coordinates = 22.90 |coordinates = 140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 27.00 |omitted = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |BurialStructure = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |built = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |ImperialTomb = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |SpecialNotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designated as a National other_designation (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designated a National other_designation in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} designation1 as a National other_designation (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !Burial Structure !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was designation1 a National other_designation in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The dimensions of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "platform," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == Burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The dimensions of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, forming a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
