File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial Structure == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 7|coordinates = 22.90 |coordinates = 140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 27.00 |omitted = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |burial = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |built = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} other_designation1 as a National other_designation (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was other_designation1 a National other_designation in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 7|coordinates = 22.90 |coordinates = 140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 27.00 |omitted = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |burial = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |built = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} other_designation1 as a National other_designation (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was other_designation1 a National other_designation in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 7|coordinates = 22.90 |coordinates = 140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 27.00 |omitted = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |burial = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |built = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} other_designation1 as a National other_designation (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was other_designation1 a National other_designation in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was other_designation1 a National other_designation in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{other_designation Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City other_designation Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 7|coordinates = 22.90 |coordinates = 140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 27.00 |omitted = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |burial = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |built = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 7|coordinates = 22.90 |coordinates = 140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 27.00 |omitted = JP-07 |type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area = Mound length: 71.8m |burial = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |burial goods = Beads, {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} |AccompanyingTombs = |built = Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|ja|白河市}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}||Late {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|ja|8世紀}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|ja|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}). == Overview ==

[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|ja|阿武隈川}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|ja|西白河郡|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 下総塚古墳 |画像 = [[File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
墳丘（左に前方部、右奥に後円部） |別名 = 瓢塚{{Sfn|舟田村（平凡社）|1993}} |所属 = |所在地 = [[福島県]][[白河市]]舟田中道114 |緯度度 = 37|緯度分 = 7|緯度秒 = 22.90 |経度度 =140|経度分 = 17|経度秒 = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |形状 = [[前方後円墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長71.8m |埋葬施設 = [[横穴式石室]] |出土品 = 玉類・[[埴輪]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[6世紀]]後半 |被葬者 = （推定）[[白河国造]] |陵墓 = |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」に包含 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図2 = {{Location map|Japan Fukushima|label=下総塚古墳|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''下総塚古墳'''（しもふさづかこふん/しもうさづかこふん）は、[[福島県]][[白河市]]舟田（ふなだ）にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+白河地域の首長墓{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}} !古墳名 !形状 !埋葬施設 !築造時期 |- |'''下総塚古墳'''||[[前方後円墳]]||[[横穴式石室]]||[[6世紀]]後半 |- |舟田中道1号墳||[[円墳]]||横穴式石室||[[7世紀]]前半-7世紀中葉 |- |[[谷地久保古墳]]||円墳||[[横口式石槨]]||7世紀後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |- |[[野地久保古墳]]||[[上円下方墳]]||横口式石槨||7世紀後半-8世紀初頭 |}
[[ファイル:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|出土埴輪}}{{small|白河市歴史民俗資料館展示。}}]] 福島県南部、[[阿武隈川]]右岸の河岸段丘上に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。古くは[[江戸時代]]の『白河風土記』に記載が見える。現在までに墳丘は大きく削平を受けているほか、[[1932年]]（[[昭和]]7年）に石室測量調査が、[[1996年]]（[[平成]]8年）以降に発掘調査が実施されている{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を西方向に向ける。墳丘周囲には幅9-15メートル・深さ1.2メートルの周濠が巡らされ、周濠内からは[[円筒埴輪]]・[[形象埴輪]]（人物形・盾形・大刀形・翳形・家形・動物形埴輪）が検出されている{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]で、南南西方向に開口した。石室内は盗掘に遭っており副葬品の大部分は失われているが、発掘調査では切子玉・ガラス玉が検出されている{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 この下総塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]後半頃の築造と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。北西150メートルの舟田中道遺跡で検出された豪族居館（6世紀後半-[[7世紀]]前半）とともに、古代[[白河郡]]の成立直前の勢力の存在を示唆しており、『[[先代旧事本紀]]』「[[国造本紀]]」に見える[[白河国造]]との関連が推測される。また、下総塚古墳・舟田中道遺跡は北方にある[[終末期古墳]]の[[谷地久保古墳]]・[[野地久保古墳]]とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、白河地域の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2015年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」のうち）。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[文化 (元号)|文化]]2年（[[1805年]]）編纂の『白河風土記』に「東西二十間、南北五間、高さ二間」として記載{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1932年]]（[[昭和]]7年）、石室測量調査（岩越二郎、[[1936年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1996年|1996]]-[[1997年]]（[[平成]]8-9年）、県営圃場整備に伴う範囲確認調査（白河市教育委員会、[[1997年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2000年|2000]]-[[2002年]]（平成12-14年）、整備に伴う発掘調査：第4-6次調査（白河市教育委員会、[[2001年|2001]]-[[2003年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2015年]]（平成17年）7月14日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り。 * 墳丘長：71.8メートル - 1996-1997年の調査時点では62メートルとされた{{Sfn|下総塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 後円部 直径：45.4メートル * 前方部 幅：63.3メートル 墳丘の1段目は「基壇」とも呼ばれる幅広いもので、下野地域によく見られる特徴になる{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 なお、かつて古墳時代後期としては東北地方で最大規模の古墳とされたが{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}、近年では[[塚前古墳]]（[[いわき市]]、6世紀中頃）の方が上回る規模であることが判明している。 File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|後円部墳頂 File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|前方部から後円部を望む File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|後円部から前方部を望む == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南南西方向に開口した。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 石室全長：7.1メートル * 幅：奥壁部1.94メートル、入り口部1.14メートル * 高さ：奥壁2.1メートル、残存側壁1.5メートル 石室は奥壁から入り口にかけて狭くなる羽子板状の平面形を呈する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。側壁の背面には10センチメートル程度の裏込め石が認められる{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、入り口付近では両側壁の間に川原石が詰まった状態で検出され、閉塞石と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 石室内は盗掘に遭っているが、発掘調査では切子玉・ガラス玉が検出されている{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 ファイル:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|切子玉
{{small|白河市歴史民俗資料館展示。}} == 関連施設 == * 白河市歴史民俗資料館（白河市中田） - 下総塚古墳出土品等を保管・展示。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（白河市教育委員会設置） * 地方自治体発行 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2011|chapter=|title=国指定史跡 白河舟田・本沼遺跡群 白河官衙遺跡群（白河市文化財パンフレット）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}}} * 事典類 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1993|chapter=舟田村|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 7 福島県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490077|ref={{Harvid|舟田村（平凡社）|1993}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=川崎純徳|year=1989|chapter=下総塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|下総塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=鈴木功|year=2002|chapter=下総塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|下総塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=|chapter=[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%99%BD%E6%B2%B3%E8%88%9F%E7%94%B0-%E6%9C%AC%E6%B2%BC%E9%81%BA%E8%B7%A1%E7%BE%A4-1444165 白河舟田-本沼遺跡群]|title=国指定史跡ガイド|publisher=[[講談社]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|白河舟田-本沼遺跡群（国指定史跡）}}}} - リンクは[[朝日新聞社]]「[[コトバンク]]」。 == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite journal|和書|author=岩越二郎|title=西白河郡烏峠付近の遺蹟遺物に就いて（上）|date=1936|publisher=岩磐郷土研究会|journal=岩磐史談|volume=|number=7|pages=|url=|naid=|doi=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1997|chapter=|title=下総塚古墳 -市内遺跡詳細分布調査報告書-（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第20集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2001|chapter=|title=下総塚古墳発掘調査報告書 第4次調査（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第30集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2002|chapter=|title=下総塚古墳発掘調査報告書 第5次調査（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第35集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2003|chapter=|title=下総塚古墳発掘調査報告書 第6次調査（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第39集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=鈴木功|year=2006|chapter=|title=白河郡衙遺跡群 -古代東国行政の一大中心地-（日本の遺跡10）|publisher=[[同成社]]|isbn=4886213545|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2017|chapter=|title=史跡白河舟田・本沼遺跡群、白河官衙遺跡群保存活用計画書|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]] ** [[谷地久保古墳]] ** [[野地久保古墳]] * [[白河国造]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Shimofusazuka Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} * [http://www.city.shirakawa.fukushima.jp/sp/page/page001388.html 白河舟田・本沼遺跡群 > 下総塚古墳] - {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 下総塚古墳 |画像 = [[File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
墳丘（左に前方部、右奥に後円部） |別名 = 瓢塚{{Sfn|舟田村（平凡社）|1993}} |所属 = |所在地 = [[福島県]][[白河市]]舟田中道114 |緯度度 = 37|緯度分 = 7|緯度秒 = 22.90 |経度度 =140|経度分 = 17|経度秒 = 27.00 |ISO = JP-07 |形状 = [[前方後円墳]] |規模 = 墳丘長71.8m |埋葬施設 = [[横穴式石室]] |出土品 = 玉類・[[埴輪]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[6世紀]]後半 |被葬者 = （推定）[[白河国造]] |陵墓 = |史跡 = 国の[[史跡]]「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」に包含 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図2 = {{Location map|Japan Fukushima|label=下総塚古墳|lat_deg=37|lat_min=7|lat_sec=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''下総塚古墳'''（しもふさづかこふん/しもうさづかこふん）は、[[福島県]][[白河市]]舟田（ふなだ）にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+白河地域の首長墓{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}} !古墳名 !形状 !埋葬施設 !築造時期 |- |'''下総塚古墳'''||[[前方後円墳]]||[[横穴式石室]]||[[6世紀]]後半 |- |舟田中道1号墳||[[円墳]]||横穴式石室||[[7世紀]]前半-7世紀中葉 |- |[[谷地久保古墳]]||円墳||[[横口式石槨]]||7世紀後半-[[8世紀]]初頭 |- |[[野地久保古墳]]||[[上円下方墳]]||横口式石槨||7世紀後半-8世紀初頭 |}
[[ファイル:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|出土埴輪}}{{small|白河市歴史民俗資料館展示。}}]] 福島県南部、[[阿武隈川]]右岸の河岸段丘上に築造された古墳である{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。古くは[[江戸時代]]の『白河風土記』に記載が見える。現在までに墳丘は大きく削平を受けているほか、[[1932年]]（[[昭和]]7年）に石室測量調査が、[[1996年]]（[[平成]]8年）以降に発掘調査が実施されている{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 墳形は前方後円形で、前方部を西方向に向ける。墳丘周囲には幅9-15メートル・深さ1.2メートルの周濠が巡らされ、周濠内からは[[円筒埴輪]]・[[形象埴輪]]（人物形・盾形・大刀形・翳形・家形・動物形埴輪）が検出されている{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]で、南南西方向に開口した。石室内は盗掘に遭っており副葬品の大部分は失われているが、発掘調査では切子玉・ガラス玉が検出されている{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 この下総塚古墳は、[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]後半頃の築造と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。北西150メートルの舟田中道遺跡で検出された豪族居館（6世紀後半-[[7世紀]]前半）とともに、古代[[白河郡]]の成立直前の勢力の存在を示唆しており、『[[先代旧事本紀]]』「[[国造本紀]]」に見える[[白河国造]]との関連が推測される。また、下総塚古墳・舟田中道遺跡は北方にある[[終末期古墳]]の[[谷地久保古墳]]・[[野地久保古墳]]とともに古墳時代の[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]として認知され、周辺に展開する[[関和久官衙遺跡]]（推定白河郡衙跡）・[[借宿廃寺跡]]からなる古代の白河官衙遺跡群と合わせて、白河地域の中心地を示す遺跡群の一角として重要視される古墳である。 古墳域は[[2015年]]（平成17年）に国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「白河舟田・本沼遺跡群」のうち）。 == 遺跡歴 == * [[文化 (元号)|文化]]2年（[[1805年]]）編纂の『白河風土記』に「東西二十間、南北五間、高さ二間」として記載{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1932年]]（[[昭和]]7年）、石室測量調査（岩越二郎、[[1936年]]に報告）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[1996年|1996]]-[[1997年]]（[[平成]]8-9年）、県営圃場整備に伴う範囲確認調査（白河市教育委員会、[[1997年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2000年|2000]]-[[2002年]]（平成12-14年）、整備に伴う発掘調査：第4-6次調査（白河市教育委員会、[[2001年|2001]]-[[2003年]]に報告書刊行）{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * [[2015年]]（平成17年）7月14日、国の[[史跡]]に指定（史跡「[[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]]」のうち）{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}}。 == 墳丘 == 墳丘の規模は次の通り。 * 墳丘長：71.8メートル - 1996-1997年の調査時点では62メートルとされた{{Sfn|下総塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 後円部 直径：45.4メートル * 前方部 幅：63.3メートル 墳丘の1段目は「基壇」とも呼ばれる幅広いもので、下野地域によく見られる特徴になる{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 なお、かつて古墳時代後期としては東北地方で最大規模の古墳とされたが{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}、近年では[[塚前古墳]]（[[いわき市]]、6世紀中頃）の方が上回る規模であることが判明している。 File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|後円部墳頂 File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|前方部から後円部を望む File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|後円部から前方部を望む == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南南西方向に開口した。石室の規模は次の通り{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 * 石室全長：7.1メートル * 幅：奥壁部1.94メートル、入り口部1.14メートル * 高さ：奥壁2.1メートル、残存側壁1.5メートル 石室は奥壁から入り口にかけて狭くなる羽子板状の平面形を呈する{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。側壁の背面には10センチメートル程度の裏込め石が認められる{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。また、入り口付近では両側壁の間に川原石が詰まった状態で検出され、閉塞石と推定される{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 石室内は盗掘に遭っているが、発掘調査では切子玉・ガラス玉が検出されている{{Sfn|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}。 ファイル:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|切子玉
{{small|白河市歴史民俗資料館展示。}} == 関連施設 == * 白河市歴史民俗資料館（白河市中田） - 下総塚古墳出土品等を保管・展示。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（白河市教育委員会設置） * 地方自治体発行 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2011|chapter=|title=国指定史跡 白河舟田・本沼遺跡群 白河官衙遺跡群（白河市文化財パンフレット）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|白河市文化財パンフレット|2011}}}} * 事典類 ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1993|chapter=舟田村|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 7 福島県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490077|ref={{Harvid|舟田村（平凡社）|1993}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=川崎純徳|year=1989|chapter=下総塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|下総塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=鈴木功|year=2002|chapter=下総塚古墳|title=[[日本古墳大辞典|続 日本古墳大辞典]]|publisher=[[東京堂出版]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|下総塚古墳（続古墳）|2002}}}} ** {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=|chapter=[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%99%BD%E6%B2%B3%E8%88%9F%E7%94%B0-%E6%9C%AC%E6%B2%BC%E9%81%BA%E8%B7%A1%E7%BE%A4-1444165 白河舟田-本沼遺跡群]|title=国指定史跡ガイド|publisher=[[講談社]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|白河舟田-本沼遺跡群（国指定史跡）}}}} - リンクは[[朝日新聞社]]「[[コトバンク]]」。 == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite journal|和書|author=岩越二郎|title=西白河郡烏峠付近の遺蹟遺物に就いて（上）|date=1936|publisher=岩磐郷土研究会|journal=岩磐史談|volume=|number=7|pages=|url=|naid=|doi=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1997|chapter=|title=下総塚古墳 -市内遺跡詳細分布調査報告書-（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第20集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2001|chapter=|title=下総塚古墳発掘調査報告書 第4次調査（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第30集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2002|chapter=|title=下総塚古墳発掘調査報告書 第5次調査（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第35集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2003|chapter=|title=下総塚古墳発掘調査報告書 第6次調査（白河市埋蔵文化財調査報告書 第39集）|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=鈴木功|year=2006|chapter=|title=白河郡衙遺跡群 -古代東国行政の一大中心地-（日本の遺跡10）|publisher=[[同成社]]|isbn=4886213545|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2017|chapter=|title=史跡白河舟田・本沼遺跡群、白河官衙遺跡群保存活用計画書|publisher=白河市教育委員会|isbn=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[白河舟田・本沼遺跡群]] ** [[谷地久保古墳]] ** [[野地久保古墳]] * [[白河国造]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Shimofusazuka Kofun}} * {{国指定文化財等データベース|401|00003447|白河舟田・本沼遺跡群}} * [http://www.city.shirakawa.fukushima.jp/sp/page/page001388.html 白河舟田・本沼遺跡群 > 下総塚古墳] - Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = [[:en:Shirakawa, Fukushima|Shirakawa, Fukushima]] Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 7|coordinates = 22.90 |coordinates = 140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 27.00 |omitted = JP-07 |type = [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] |area = Mound length: 71.8m |burial = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |burial goods = Beads, [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] |subsidiary sites = |built = Late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group]] |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Shirakawa, Fukushima|Shirakawa, Fukushima]] Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]] |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}||Late 7th to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==

Mound (front section on the left, rear circular section in the right background) |alternate_name = Hyoutan-zuka{{Sfn|Funada Village (Heibonsha)|1993}} |part_of = |location = [[:en:Shirakawa, Fukushima|Shirakawa, Fukushima]] Funada Nakamichi 114, [[Fukushima Prefecture]] |coordinates = 37|coordinates = 7|coordinates = 22.90 |coordinates = 140|coordinates = 17|coordinates = 27.00 |omitted = JP-07 |type = [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] |area = Mound length: 71.8m |burial = {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |burial goods = Beads, [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] |subsidiary sites = |built = Late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] |InterredIndividual = (Presumed) {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} |Mausoleum = |HistoricalSite = Included in the National [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group]] |CulturalAssets = |Specialnotes = |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|map_dot_label=Shimofusazuka Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Shirakawa, Fukushima|Shirakawa, Fukushima]] Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the [[:en:Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites]]). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late [[:en:6th century|6th century]] |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]] |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}||Late 7th to early [[:en:8th century|8th century]] |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the [[:en:Abukuma River|Abukuma River]] in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient [[:en:Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|Shirakawa District]]. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}} == Related Facilities == * Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum (Shirakawa City Nakata) - Stores and displays burial goods
