Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|en|Shirakawa, Fukushima|WD=Q750587|lt=Shirakawa, Fukushima}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cave Tomb-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Cave Tomb-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}} == Related Facilities == * Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum (Shirakawa City Nakata) - Stores and displays burial goods from Shimofusazuka Kofun. == References == {{Reflist}} == Sources == {{small|(Sources used for article composition)}} * Explanatory signboard (installed by Shirakawa City Board of Education) * Local Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|en|Shirakawa, Fukushima|WD=Q750587|lt=Shirakawa, Fukushima}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}}). == Overview ==

[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District}}. Kofun|coordinates=37|coordinates=7|coordinates=22.90|lon_deg=140|lon_min=17|lon_sec=27.00|mark=前方後円墳-西.svg|marksize=28|float=center|border=none|position=bottom|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Shimofusazuka Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|en|Shirakawa, Fukushima|WD=Q750587|lt=Shirakawa, Fukushima}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoanabo-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}} == Related Facilities == * Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum (Shirakawa City Nakata) - Stores and displays burial goods Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|en|Shirakawa, Fukushima|WD=Q750587|lt=Shirakawa, Fukushima}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoanabo-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|en|Shirakawa, Fukushima|WD=Q750587|lt=Shirakawa, Fukushima|1=Shirakawa, Fukushima}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|1=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century|1=8th century}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoanabo-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River|1=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|1=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}}). == Overview ==

[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River|1=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River|1=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. Kofun''' (下総塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|en|Shirakawa, Fukushima|WD=Q750587|lt=Shirakawa, Fukushima|1=Shirakawa, Fukushima}} Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|1=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century|1=8th century}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoanabo-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River|1=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads

Funada (舟田), Fukushima Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Zenpōkōenfun|en|Zenpōkōenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpōkōenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (part of the {{ill|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|en|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|WD=Q11579979|lt=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites|1=Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Sites}}). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+ Chief Tombs of the Shirakawa Region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}} !Tomb name !type !burial burial !built |- |'''Shimofusazuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Zenpōkōenfun|en|Zenpōkōenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpōkōenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}||{{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}||Late {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}} |- |Funada Nakamichi No. 1 Kofun||{{ill|Round kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoana-style stone chamber||Early to mid-{{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} |- |{{ill|Yachikubo Kofun|ja|谷地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yachikubo Kofun|qq=}}||Round kofun||{{ill|Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoanabo-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}||Late 7th to early {{ill|8th century|en|8th century|WD=Q8086|lt=8th century|1=8th century}} |- |{{ill|Nojikubo Kofun|ja|野地久保古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nojikubo Kofun|qq=}}||{{ill|Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|lt=Joenkahofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Yokoanabo-style stone chamber||Late 7th to early 8th century |}
[[File:下総塚古墳出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Haniwa unearthed from Shimofusazuka Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at the Shirakawa City History and Folklore Museum.}}]] Located on the river terrace along the right bank of the {{ill|Abukuma River|en|Abukuma River|WD=Q335853|lt=Abukuma River|1=Abukuma River}} in southern Fukushima Prefecture, the kofun was recorded in the Edo period document *Shirakawa Fudoki*. The mound has undergone significant leveling over time. Measured surveys of the stone chamber were conducted in 1932 (Showa 7), and archaeological excavations were carried out from 1996 (Heisei 8) onwards{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The mound is keyhole-shaped, with the front section oriented west. A moat approximately 9–15 meters wide and 1.2 meters deep encircles the mound, and various {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} types (cylindrical, human, shield, sword, fan, house, and animal-shaped) have been recovered from within the moat{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} that opens to the south-southwest. Despite being looted, excavations have uncovered cut-glass and glass beads{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The kofun is estimated to have been built in the late 6th century{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Along with the aristocratic residence found at the Funada Nakamichi site 150 meters northwest (dating to the late 6th to early 7th century), it is thought to indicate the presence of a significant regional power just before the establishment of ancient {{ill|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|en|Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima|WD=Q1155789|lt=Shirakawa District|1=Nishishirakawa District, Fukushima}}. The kofun is also linked to the {{ill|Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|白河国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shirakawa Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} mentioned in the *Sendai Kuji Hongi* "Kuni no Miyatsuko Hongi"{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. The site was Historic Site1 a National Historic Site in 2015 (part of the Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group){{Historic Site Online Database|401|00003447|Shirakawa Funada-Motonuma Archaeological Sites Group}}. == Mound area == The area of the mound are as follows: * Mound length: 71.8 meters (62 meters based on 1996–1997 surveys){{Sfn|Shimofusazuka Kofun (Revised Kofun Dictionary)|2002}}{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. * Rear circular section diameter: 45.4 meters * Front section width: 63.3 meters The first tier of the mound, often called a "plattype," is a broad feature commonly seen in the Shimotsuke region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although once considered the largest kofun of the late Kofun period in the Tohoku region{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}, recent studies indicate the {{ill|Tsukamae Kofun|ja|塚前古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamae Kofun|qq=}} (Iwaki City, mid-6th century) surpasses it in map_size. File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, funcho.jpg|Top of the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, kouenbu.jpg|View from the front section toward the rear circular section File:Shimofusazuka Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|View from the rear circular section toward the front section == burial burial == The burial structure is a {{ill|Yokoana-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} opening to the south-southwest. The area of the chamber are as follows{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}: * Total chamber length: 7.1 meters * Width: Rear wall 1.94 meters, entrance 1.14 meters * Height: Rear wall 2.1 meters, surviving side walls 1.5 meters The chamber narrows from the rear wall toward the entrance, typeing a paddle-shaped floor plan{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Approximately 10 cm of backfill stones are present behind the side walls{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. At the entrance, cobblestones were discovered between the side walls, likely functioning as closure stones{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. Although looted, cut-glass and glass beads were recovered during excavations{{Sfn|Shirakawa City Historic Site Pamphlet|2011}}. File:下総塚古墳出土 切子玉.JPG|Cut-glass beads
